sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Primary Objective**: Increase forest/tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha) and improve quality of forest cover on another 5 mha. 
• **Total Target**: 10 million hectares of forest/tree cover improvement. 
• **Core Philosophy**: Shift from purely 'production-based' forestry to 'ecosystem-based' forestry, emphasizing biodiversity, water, and biomass. 
• **Key Metric**: Carbon sequestration target of 50-60 million tonnes of CO2 annually by 2020 (now integrated into broader NDC targets).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Focuses on entire landscapes (watersheds/ecosystems) rather than isolated patches.
Integrated management of forest and non-forest lands.
Mains: Essential for 'Integrated Landscape Management' questions.
Gram Sabhas and Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) as primary implementers.
Decentralized governance and local livelihood integration.
Prelims: Focus on the role of local institutions in climate adaptation.

items.definition: Forests act as carbon sinks; GIM aims to enhance this capacity to mitigate climate change impacts.
Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority; often used for convergence with GIM activities.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Convergence**: GIM is designed to converge with MGNREGA, CAMPA, and National Afforestation Programme (NAP). 
• **Ecosystem Services**: Focus on water security, soil conservation, and non-timber forest produce (NTFP).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Land availability, conflict between developmental projects and forest conservation, and monitoring of survival rates of saplings. 
• **Solutions**: Use of GIS/Remote Sensing for real-time monitoring and 'Green Credits' system.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: '5+5=10' 
• **Decoded Meaning**: 5 million hectares (New cover) + 5 million hectares (Improved quality) = 10 million hectares total target.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: GIM is NOT just about planting trees; it is about 'improving the quality' of existing forests. Do not confuse it with simple afforestation drives.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Nature-based Solutions (NbS)' when discussing GIM in the context of climate change mitigation.

keyTakeaways: GIM is a landscape-based approach, not a site-specific plantation drive.
It emphasizes the role of local communities (Gram Sabhas) in forest governance.
It is a critical component of India's NDC commitment to create an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2030.
